ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence must be completed before filing. Every shareholder holding 10% or more of the economic interest and every ultimate beneficial owner must be screened against Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit databases, Central Bank of Egypt consolidated sanction lists, the Office of Foreign Assets Control Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions list, European Union and United Kingdom consolidated financial sanction lists, and domestic Egyptian asset-freezing lists issued by the National Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Committee. For ISIC 6499 blank-check and special purpose acquisition companies, the protocol additionally requires bank-attested source of funds evidence, adverse media search, UBO and politically exposed person relationship screening covering family members and close associates, and written risk acceptance by the Egyptian compliance officer or legal counsel before incorporation. Identification of a politically exposed person triggers high-risk onboarding with board level approval and mandatory enhanced periodic review at least every 180 days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Electronic Company Name Reservation and Commercial Registry Portal (www.gafi.gov.eg / investinegypt.gov.eg), administered by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The primary legal name of the Egyptian LLC must be submitted in Arabic. A phonetic Arabic-Latin transliteration may be registered as an auxiliary commercial name provided it corresponds faithfully to the Arabic name and does not create a materially different enterprise. The legal form suffix L.L.C. or Limited Liability Company must appear in the name. Foreign-language names may be accepted only as auxiliary names and must not imply regulated banking, insurance, securities, sovereign, military or state-linked activity unless the relevant competent authority has issued prior written approval.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended once for an additional 30 days by filing GAFI Form N-ER before the original expiry date and paying the statutory extension tariff. Upon rejection, the applicant receives a reasoned refusal notice. An administrative grievance must be filed with the GAFI Commercial Name Clearance Committee within 15 business days of rejection, attaching the refusal notice, the proposed alternative transliteration and supporting commercial registry search evidence. If the Committee denies the grievance, an appeal may be filed with the GAFI Board Grievance Committee within 30 days. A further annulment action may be brought before the Cairo Administrative Court within 60 days of the board-level denial. The applicant may simultaneously reserve one alternative name in a separate filing without forfeiting priority under the original reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual mailbox is not acceptable as the registered office of an Egyptian SPAC LLC. GAFI and the Commercial Registry require a genuine physical office address in Egypt for service of process, maintenance of statutory minute books and records, inspection of the UBO and economic ownership register by competent authorities, and retention of corporate documentation. A serviced or compliance-grade office in Cairo, Alexandria, or the Suez Canal Economic Zone may satisfy the requirement if it includes a dedicated physical suite, Arabic nameplate, valid lease, meeting accommodation, and a responsible resident agent; a non-exclusive virtual office will be rejected at registration or during post-incorporation inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Elevated. For blank-check and special purpose acquisition vehicles classified under ISIC 6499, GAFI and the Egyptian AML Financial Intelligence Unit treat the entity as medium-risk enhanced. The estimated likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection is approximately 70% within the first 24 months after incorporation. Inspections verify physical occupancy, corporate minute books, the UBO and economic ownership register, capitalization records, auditor appointment, and compliance with registered office obligations. Denial of access may trigger administrative referral, licence suspension and forced entry by an administrative bailiff.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as subsequently amended) — Part II on Limited Liability Companies; Executive Regulations issued by Ministry of Economy Decree No. 96 of 1982, as amended; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976; Capital Market Law No. 95 of 1992 for the FRA authorization.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — One-Stop-Shop (OSS), coordinated with the Commercial Registry Directorate.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (Form 1-LLC) filed through the GAFI online portal, together with the notarized Articles of Association and the bank certificate for the paid-in capital deposited in the blocked trust escrow account.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital (metadata flag: false). The founding members must, nevertheless, pay the subscribed capital in cash into a blocked escrow account with a Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) licensed bank; for a SPAC, the escrow balance must equal the offering proceeds and comply with FRA trust rules, with no withdrawal before 24 months unless FRA authorizes an extension or a qualifying acquisition.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRSTLY, that the founding members adopt the Memorandum and Articles of Association of the blank-check acquisition vehicle incorporated under Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended; RESOLVED SECONDLY, that the registered office is fixed at the address notified to GAFI, Egypt; RESOLVED THIRDLY, that the subscribed capital is fully paid into a blocked escrow account held with a Central-Bank-of-Egypt-licensed bank; RESOLVED FOURTHLY, that Mr./Ms. [Name] is appointed General Manager with full power before third parties; RESOLVED FINALLY, that the General Manager is authorized to file the incorporation application, procure the commercial registration, tax card, FRA license and civil-defense clearances, open bank accounts, and sign all ancillary instruments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the Company Name and Pre-Clear SPAC Scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop-Shop — Trade Name Acquisition Unit, Cairo Head Office (electronic portal: www.gafi.gov.eg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a trade-name reservation request with three alternative Arabic/English transliterations via the GAFI portal. The OSS checks the Commercial Registry name index and disqualifies names identical or confusingly similar to existing registrations, names with religious connotations, or names incompatible with Law 159/1981. Upon clearance, the name is reserved for 30 days and may be renewed once.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID copy of each founding member
Notarized power of attorney of the local legal delegate (if any)
Three proposed company names in Latin and Arabic script
Short narrative of the proposed SPAC acquisition strategy for GAFI pre-clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file an administrative appeal before the GAFI Legal Department within 15 days, or provide a notarial no-objection letter from the owner of the conflicting name.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Cairo; electronic portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg (unified tax registration and e-filing platform).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing an Egyptian LLC must first obtain legal existence through the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) incorporation procedure, then apply to the Egyptian Tax Authority for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) using the unified tax registration form. For VAT purposes, the same TIN serves as the VAT ID. The ETA registration requires the entity's constitutional documents, power of attorney for the local tax representative, proof of Egyptian registered address, and identification of legal persons/shareholders. Registration must be completed within 30 days of incorporation. A tax card (Bayan Card) is issued, consolidating CIT, VAT, and payroll tax registrations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not operate a check-the-box classification system. Entity level taxation is mandatory for an Egyptian LLC. Elections available include: (i) application of double taxation treaty relief on foreign income; (ii) election to attribute VAT input tax using the standard credit mechanism; (iii) election under investment incentive regimes (e.g., Special Economic Zones of Suez Canal) for certain tax holidays or exemptions; (iv) declaration to apply the simplified presumptive taxation scheme, if eligible. Hybrid mismatch elections are not recognized under Egyptian domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover; mandatory VAT registration is triggered when the value of taxable supplies of goods and services exceeds EGP 500,000 per calendar year.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic e-invoicing is phased in across all B2B transactions. Taxpayers must submit invoice data in real time to the ETA e-invoice system via HTTPS RESTful APIs with digital signature (XML/JSON schema), obtaining a Unique Identifier (UUID) from the ETA for each invoice before issuance to the buyer. Clearance is automated with a maximum of 15 seconds per invoice. E-receipts are mandated for B2C sales. Taxpayers must operate an API middleware through an accredited electronic invoicing service provider or direct integration. Digital stamping of invoices is replaced by the real-time clearance validation. Non-compliance blocks invoice issuance and triggers fines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under the Egyptian VAT Law applies to: (i) goods physically exported outside Egypt, with proof of actual customs exit; (ii) supplies of goods to free zones and special economic zones if qualifying; (iii) international transport of goods or passengers; (iv) services directly related to exported goods or international transport, carried out and delivered to non-residents; and (v) goods or services sold to foreign-flagged vessels and aircraft. The exporter must hold all shipping, customs, payment, and commercial evidence demonstrating that the goods left Egypt and that the consideration was received from a non-resident.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (outward clearance approved by Egyptian Customs)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill / Road Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit document evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA and Central Bank of Egypt conduct post-shipment audits of export zero-rating claims. If zero-rating is claimed without actual physical export, proper customs documentation, or timely repatriation of export proceeds, the VAT becomes immediately due at 14%, plus late payment interest calculated daily using the Central Bank discount rate plus 2 percentage points, and a penalty not exceeding the amount of tax evaded. In cases of deliberate fraud or false declarations, administrative penalties range from EGP 20,000 to EGP 100,000, with criminal liability including imprisonment under Egyptian VAT Law No. 67 of 2016. Retrospective clawback may cover the preceding five tax years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), acting through the General Foreign Exchange Administration, the Banking Supervision Sector, and the Foreign Exchange Operations Committee. The statutory basis is the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020, together with the Egyptian Foreign Exchange Law No. 38 of 1992 as applicable. The CBE exclusively licenses banks, approves capital account transfers, supervises bank SWIFT/FX operations, and issues binding circulars on inward and outward remittance documentation, nostro/vostro account operations, and usage of Egyptian pound and foreign currency accounts by resident and non-resident legal persons.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The EGP is formally convertible in the interbank market, with a market-determined exchange rate managed by CBE interventions during exceptional volatility. Current-account transactions for trade, services, and repatriation of after-tax profits are generally permitted without individual CBE permits, provided the full documentary chain is processed through a licensed Egyptian bank. Capital-account transactions are convertible subject to CBE complaint, including the registration of foreign participation under the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017. Profit and dividend remittance by an Egyptian LLC is legally unconditional but operationally requires: audited financial statements, tax registration certificate and tax clearance from the Egyptian Tax Authority, the general meeting's distribution resolution, beneficial ownership declarations, and a formal remittance request signed by the authorized bank signatories. In periods of FX reserve pressure, CBE may impose bank-level priority queues and settlement sequencing, but no general ban on profit remittance exists for compliant entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For any export-influenced inflow to the Egyptian LLC, CBE-licensed banks require full export proceeds to be repatriated to Egypt within 90 days from the date of shipment or earlier if the underlying letter of credit requires; banks must receive the foreign currency amount and credit it to the exporter's export proceeds account. After the 2016 liberalisation there is no fixed mandatory surrender ratio; exporters may retain the foreign currency in a bank-held account or convert at the prevailing market rate, but 100% of the proceeds must be booked in Egypt. The documentary compliance package includes the commodity import/export declaration, commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, and bank foreign receipt. Non-utilisation or set-off without bank consent is prohibited. A pure blank-check and acquisition vehicle that does not itself undertake commercial exports has no standing export surrender obligation unless the target operating company is an Egyptian exporter, in which case the CBE circulars apply at the Egyptian operating entity level.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.capital_controls_margin_note: The CBE maintains a suspension/blocking mechanism for transactions involving sanctioned persons, shell counterparties, or suspicious source-of-funds. Foreign exchange hedging and derivative transactions are confined to real-economy or investment-backed risk, and speculative positional FX trading is not permitted for the Egyptian LLC.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for offshore EMI or non-bank fintech providers as primary treasury rails. Under Law No. 194 of 2020, deposit-taking and payment account issuance are restricted to licensed banks and regulated fintech payment institutions supervised by CBE. An offshore digital EMI cannot lawfully hold EGP client balances, open an Egyptian resident LLC operating account, or provide escrow services without partnering with an Egyptian bank or obtaining a CBE/Non-Bank Financial Regulatory Authority license. An offshore SWIFT-connected B2B platform may support ancillary receivables, but the capital injection, trust escrow, and M&A disbursement flows must be cleared through a licensed Egyptian licensed bank and correspond through the standard nostro network.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person or bank-supervised video KYC is mandatory for all non-retail legal entity accounts. For an Egyptian LLC, at least one locally resident director or authorised Egyptian manager must attend the onboarding interview physically at a CBE-licensed branch; foreign founders must provide either a physically signed and notarised board resolution witnessed by an Egyptian consulate or a power of attorney issued to the Egyptian-appointed director, together with an apostille in common-law jurisdictions. Fully remote opening without any physical Egyptian presence is not accepted for a blank-check entity because of the enhanced AML classification. Existing bank clients may use video KYC only after a substantive in-person interview of the UBO and local signatory has been completed and the bank’s AML officer has accepted the risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The SPAC / blank-check classification qualifies as enhanced-risk investment vehicle, generating Medium-Risk Enhanced due diligence under CBE AML/CTF rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified SPAC organisational documents, trust/escrow agreement, sponsor contribution ledger, US/Egypt counsel legal opinions, a structural trust chart identifying each ultimate beneficial owner over 25%, the FATF-based risk matrix, and a written statement of the intended public-market acquisition strategy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The inbound investment originates from jurisdictions that the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit or CBE may view as high-risk or non-cooperative territories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete SWIFT chain illustrating origination from a regulated bank, investor source-of-funds statements, tax identification certificates, licensed counsel identity attestation, sanctions-list screening results from a participating Egyptian bank, and a false-positive resolution report where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The LLC has minimal operating history, no local employees, and a non-resident board, thus triggering a transactional/corporate shell suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial registration extract, tax card, occupancy/lease certificate for registered office in Egypt, Egyptian licensed accountant appointment, audited annual financial statements or capital-ledger confirmation, minutes of board resolutions, and the ISIC-6499 authorization letter issued by the investment authority confirming approved SPAC purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital arrives through third-party attorney trust accounts or an intermediate SPAC vehicle, creating opacity on the actual account owner and source-of-funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contractual fund-flow memorandum, signed subscription and closing agreements, bank letters confirming underlying investors, source-of-funds certification, legal undertaking executed by Egyptian counsel, pricing and valuation report of the target, and a mirror structure of each trust account holding funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The sole compliant inward route for foreign equity capital is via SWIFT MT103 from the investor’s bank to the Egyptian licensed bank’s nostro account, with beneficiary being the LLC’s capital escrow account. The remittance must substantively identify the underlying acquisition or SPAC capital subscription in the narrative field and be treated as a capital-account injection, not as a trade payment. The Egyptian bank will verify the letter of approval from Egypt’s investment authority, the LLC’s final capitalization table, the share subscription resolution, and the CBE’s beneficial ownership form. In practice the bank may require the funds to be preliminarily credited to a suspense account pending confirmation of the subscription ledger and the issuance of updated commercial registry records. For technical settlement, the LLC should direct the remitting bank to use the purpose code for acquisition of local equities or capital increase, or the CBE bank-specific remittance reason code used for Foreign Direct Investment, and must ensure that no cash proceeds are released until the escrow restrictions and anti-money laundering conditions are satisfied.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for SPAC acquisition costs, trust contributions, legal advisor fees, notarial costs, and target securities settlement should be executed by SWIFT MT103 for direct third-party payments, SWIFT MT202 COV for interbank transfers between Egyptian banks and global correspondent banks, and documentary commercial letters of credit or standby letters of credit where the Egyptian operating treasury is purchasing goods or securing earn-out obligations. The bank requires the full underlying contract, tax invoice, corporate resolution, target closing statement, and CBE remittance request form. Any outbound payment to the target company’s warranty/escrow account must be disability? More accurately must identify the beneficiary trust account and be accompanied by the relevant escrow release instruction and tax withholdings.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable EGP-USD forward contracts executed with an Egyptian licensed bank for a genuine underlying capital injection, acquisition payment, or divestment repatriation, with tenors aligned to transaction cash flows.
FX currency swaps between USD and EGP with an Egyptian licensed bank for cash-flow timing when the LLC has matched contractual inflows and outflows, subject to bank credit limits and CBE reporting.

Cross-currency swap structures used to hedge the foreign currency exposure of an asset purchase in the target jurisdiction where the swap is booked through the Egyptian bank’s offshore branch and wholly collateralised, with prior bank credit committee approval.

Plain-vanilla FX swap rollovers in the interbank market for management of liquidity mismatches between the capital injection date and the acquisition closing date, provided no speculative leverage is embedded.
Approved synthetic forward alternatives structured as dual-currency Islamic finance or collateralised FX swaps permitted by the licensed bank's Shariah compliance and the CBE FX governance rules.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only as a hedge by a foreign affiliate or by the local Egyptian bank acting through a licensed offshore treasury desk; the NDF must be clearly documented as a hedge of actual EGP exposure and must not create a domestic parallel market transaction in Egypt.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form for corporate taxpayers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — competent district office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end; if fiscal year ends 31 December, filing is due by 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under Income Tax Law No. 91/2005: EGP 500 for the first month plus EGP 100 for each subsequent month, commonly capped at 10% of tax due; extended delay permits the ETA to assess tax based on the taxpayer's records or third-party information, followed by enforced debt collection and manager criminal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements, managers' report, and auditor's report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Companies Registration Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: General assembly must approve annual financial statements within 6 months of fiscal year-end; filed copy must be submitted to GAFI within 30 days of approval, resulting in an outer statutory deadline of approximately 7 months after fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default under Companies Law No. 159/1981 may trigger warning letters, administrative fines, and denial of commercial licenses; failure to file audited financial statements for three consecutive years can lead to administrative dissolution and strike-off by GAFI.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial registration record renewal and tax card validity confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry (Ministry of Trade and Industry) and Egyptian Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of the commercial registration; tax-card renewal is due by 31 March each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-renewal triggers late-renewal fines, loss of legal capacity to execute contracts, suspension from government tenders, restriction on bank account operations, and eventual removal from the Commercial Register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for all Egyptian limited liability companies regardless of turnover, asset size, or number of shareholders; the general assembly must appoint a licensed certified public auditor each fiscal year under Companies Law No. 159/1981.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), which are substantially aligned with IFRS; publicly offered or Financial Regulatory Authority-supervised entities must also apply the additional FRA financial reporting rules relevant to portfolio and investment vehicles.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Egypt's beneficial ownership framework (Law No. 71/2021 and executive regulations), companies must maintain a beneficial ownership register and file updates with GAFI within 15 days of any qualifying shareholding or control change. At the annual general assembly, managers must confirm that the beneficial ownership schedule is accurate; share transfers representing 10% or more of the equity require immediate register amendment before the annual statutory filings are accepted. No standalone annual UBO return exists; the confirmation is embedded in the annual audited financial statements and the annual commercial registry renewal.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Managers and Executive Officers
Statutory Minute Book (general assembly and managers' resolutions)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% on taxable corporate income (Law 91/2005 as amended)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No broad statutory tax holiday for a passive SPAC shell; free-zone or investment incentives under Investment Law 72/2017 are available only where the entity undertakes substantive licensed industrial or service activity. A non-operating acquisition vehicle cannot lawfully claim permanent CIT exemption.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Tax Return Form No. 19 for legal persons, accompanied by Form No. 20 financial statement and tax reconciliation, filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-Tax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the close of the taxable fiscal year. For a calendar-year SPAC, the return and full payment are due on or before 30 April of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenues and gains, including trust-account interest and gains on redemption or disposal of SPAC securities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident with no Egyptian permanent establishment reports only Egypt-source gross income; treaty-exempt income is separately disclosed as exempt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses: formation, listing, escrow and trust fees, professional fees, audit costs, and documented business expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No Egyptian deductions are allowed unless the non-resident maintains a PE; PE-attributable costs must be substantiated and priced at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit after tax adjustments, computed from actual accounting records and reconciled to Egyptian tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use only Egypt-source taxable profit; submit DTA and PE analysis if claiming the absence of an Egyptian permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applied corporate tax rate and headline CIT before credits, calculated on taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the statutory 22.5% standard commercial rate; a lower DTA rate may be cited only with a valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits: advance CIT payments, withholding tax already borne on Egyptian-source income, and foreign tax credits eligible under tax treaties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach official ETA withholding certificates and foreign tax credit evidence; claim ETA refunds through a separate application for over-withheld amounts.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or late payment triggers a monthly surcharge of 2% of unpaid CIT, plus administrative fines for each unfiled statement. Repeated failure may result in automatic assessment, additional penalties of up to 100% of tax due, travel bans against responsible managers, and criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding tax on cash or in-kind dividend distributions and deemed distributions made by an Egyptian resident company to a non-resident shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must deliver a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) for the relevant year, a declaration of beneficial ownership, and the applicable DTA reduction form to the Egyptian paying entity. If the ETA has not approved the reduction at source, the payer must withhold at the statutory rate and the shareholder may file a refund claim with the ETA within the applicable limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 20% for IP royalties and interest paid to non-residents on Egyptian-source income. Under Egyptian tax treaties, royalty withholding is commonly reduced to 10-15%; interest withholding is typically 10-15%, with nil rates for certain governmental and development-financing loans and a local exemption for interest on credit facilities granted by banks licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 5,000,000 aggregate annual related-party transactions triggers the mandatory Local File; the mandatory Master File applies when the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds EGP 5,000,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt has not enacted a separate Economic Substance Regulations regime in the manner of UAE; however, treaty benefit entitlements, free-zone incentives, and anti-abuse rules require genuine commercial substance in an Egyptian SPAC: a real registered office, local governance decisions, actual employees or assets for the acquisition activity, and beneficial owners disclosed to the ETA. A shell or conduit SPAC may be disregarded, denied treaty relief, or assessed on an estimated income basis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful concealment of SPAC redemption gains, backdated transaction documents to shift profit outside Egypt, fabricated acquisition costs, false reporting on Form No. 19, or deliberate use of nominee shareholders to hide taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties under Law 91/2005: imprisonment of not less than one year and up to five years, fines of not less than 100% and up to 200% of evaded tax, automatic administrative penalty of 2% per month on unpaid tax, and immediate collection through attachment of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced where the SPAC is a mere instrumentality; directors and managers can become jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax, face travel bans and asset freezes, and may be sentenced to imprisonment for knowingly filing false returns.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a cash-shell with no commercial purpose, no local staff or premises, no board control in Egypt, or using the SPAC solely as a conduit for treaty shopping and cross-border profit stripping.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization or disregarding of the entity, denial of DTA protection, assessment of the de facto beneficial owner on a look-through basis at 22.5% CIT, plus late-payment surcharges and restitution interest from the first non-compliant period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be added as respondents to enforcement proceedings; seizure of assets and travel bans may be ordered; egregious abuse can result in disgorgement orders against shareholders who moved assets through the sham vehicle.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify and record ultimate beneficial owners of SPAC capital, accepting funds from unverified offshore or crypto sources without customer due diligence, maintaining no trust or escrow register, or disguising transfers to sanctioned persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law No. 80/2002 as amended by Law 91/2021: administrative fines up to EGP 5,000,000, confiscation of involved funds, suspension of operating licenses, deregistration of the SPAC, and criminal prosecution of compliance officers for money laundering facilitation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and AML officers face personal criminal liability, imprisonment, travel bans, and freeze orders over personal and corporate accounts where they knowingly permitted prohibited trust payments through the SPAC.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax and Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or interest to non-resident related parties without domestic WHT, applying treaty rates without a TRC, failing to file the related-party disclosure, or exceeding the EGP 5,000,000 related-party threshold without preparing a Local File and supporting arm's length analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax equal to 20% of unreported WHT plus 2% monthly late surcharges; under-reporting of profits may be corrected by the ETA using arm's length criteria, with adjustment penalties of up to 30% of the revised tax deficiency; failure to maintain documentation can result in an automatic base-default assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior tax officers can be ordered to settle unremitted WHT personally where corporate assets have been dissipated, and travel bans may be issued against responsible individuals pending full payment to the ETA.
